beats.title: Drag the triangle, watch the statements
beats.instruction: Drag vertex C to reshape the triangle. Watch which conditions are true (green) and false (red) at any moment. Try to find a position where all three sides are equal AND all three angles are equal at the same time. Try another where two sides are equal but no angle is 90°. The goal is feel, not points.
beats.successMessage: Good — you've felt the linkage between sides and angles.

steps.text: Original: 'If a polygon is a square, then it has four sides.' Hypothesis p = 'is a square'; conclusion q = 'has four sides.'
Converse (swap): 'If a polygon has four sides, then it is a square.'
Inverse (negate both): 'If a polygon is not a square, then it does not have four sides.'
Contrapositive (swap and negate): 'If a polygon does not have four sides, then it is not a square.'
Truth values: original = TRUE; converse = FALSE (rectangle is a counterexample); inverse = FALSE; contrapositive = TRUE. Original and contrapositive match; converse and inverse match.

items.prompt: In 'If a number is even, then it is divisible by 2,' what is the hypothesis?
items.explanation: The hypothesis is the 'if' part — 'a number is even.'

items.prompt: Which is the CONVERSE of 'If p, then q'?
choices: If not p, then not q.
If not q, then not p.

items.prompt: Which is the CONTRAPOSITIVE of 'If it rains, then the game is canceled'?
choices: If the game is canceled, then it rains.
If it does not rain, then the game is not canceled.
If the game is not canceled, then it does not rain.
It rains and the game is canceled.
hints: Start with 'If not q, then not p.'
q = 'game is canceled,' p = 'it rains.' So: 'If the game is not canceled, then it does not rain.'

items.prompt: Which is the INVERSE of 'If a shape is a triangle, then it has three sides'?
choices: If a shape has three sides, then it is a triangle.
If a shape is not a triangle, then it does not have three sides.
If a shape does not have three sides, then it is not a triangle.
A shape is a triangle iff it has three sides.
hints: Inverse = negate both, do not swap.
Form: 'If not p, then not q.'
Negate the hypothesis and the conclusion in place.

items.prompt: Original: 'If two angles are vertical, then they are congruent.' Truth value?
hints: This is a standard geometry theorem.
Vertical angles are the opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines.
Vertical angles are always congruent — true.

items.prompt: The converse of the statement in question 3 is 'If two angles are congruent, then they are vertical.' Truth value?
hints: Find a counterexample: two congruent angles that aren't vertical.
Two right angles on opposite ends of a room are both 90° and congruent, but they aren't vertical angles.
False — congruent angles need not be vertical.

items.prompt: A conditional and its ______ are always logically equivalent.
hints: Which derivative pairs with the original in truth value?
Original pairs with one of them; converse pairs with inverse.

testItems.prompt: In 'If a triangle is equilateral, then all sides are congruent,' what is the conclusion?
Which is the converse of 'If p, then q'?
choices: If not p, then not q.
If not q, then not p.

testItems.prompt: A statement is logically equivalent to its…
A biconditional p ⇔ q is true when…
choices: both p → q and q → p are true.
either p or q is true.

testItems.prompt: Original: 'If a quadrilateral is a rhombus, then its diagonals are perpendicular.' This is TRUE. Which of the following must also be true?
choices: If diagonals are perpendicular, then the quadrilateral is a rhombus.
If a quadrilateral is not a rhombus, then its diagonals are not perpendicular.
If diagonals are not perpendicular, then the quadrilateral is not a rhombus.
testItems.explanation: The contrapositive shares the truth value of the original.

testItems.prompt: Which definition is best written as a biconditional?
choices: A point lies on a line.
An angle is acute iff its measure is less than 90°.
testItems.explanation: Definitions work both ways: acute ⇔ measure < 90°. The others are one-directional statements or postulates.
